name: Lengthened partials / stretch training
lead: Lengthened partials are repetitions performed only in the stretched portion of an exercise, such as the bottom half of a curl, fly or pulldown, rather than through the full range of motion. Lifters use them to put the most tension on a muscle when it is at its longest, with the aim of building more muscle, for example wider shoulders, a thicker upper chest or fuller arms, which many pursue as part of a stronger physique.

The Wikipedia hypertrophy article reports that full range of motion, particularly at elongated muscle lengths, is described as enhancing growth more than partial range, and that partial-range training at long lengths is also said to promote hypertrophy, possibly through muscle damage.[1]

A 2025 randomized within-participant trial in 30 resistance-trained adults compared lengthened partials with full-range repetitions over eight weeks of upper-body training and reported similar gains in elbow flexor and extensor thickness and lat pulldown 10-rep max between the two conditions.[2]

paras: Lifters either finish a set with extra partial reps in the lengthened range or build whole sets from them. Proponents link the approach to the idea that muscles grow well when loaded at long lengths.[1] Exercises that lend themselves to it include leg extensions, curls, flies and pulldowns; T Nation members describe adding lengthened partials to leg extensions and to a physique program aimed at wider delts, a thicker upper chest and fuller triceps.[4][5]
Reviews of muscle hypertrophy describe mechanical tension as the currently accepted driver of growth and note that exercise at long muscle lengths is described as beneficial.[1]

In the 2025 PeerJ trial, 30 resistance-trained participants trained each arm with a different range of motion, lengthened partials or full range, for eight weeks. Gains in muscle thickness and 10-rep max were similar, with Bayesian analysis supporting no difference, and the authors concluded that emphasising the stretched position, whether through full range or lengthened partials, is the common factor for size.[2][6]

On T Nation the technique is discussed both enthusiastically and skeptically. One poster calls lengthened partials the latest science-based training fad, while others report using them in their own logs.[3][4][5]

One randomized trial directly compares lengthened partials with full-range training in trained participants and found similar muscle thickness and strength-endurance gains.[2][6] Reviews of resistance training and stretching examine range-of-motion improvements more broadly.[7]

timeline.event: A PeerJ randomized trial compares lengthened partials with full range of motion in 30 trained lifters.[2]

lore.intro: Lengthened partials spread through lifting communities as research on training at long muscle lengths became popular; T Nation threads show lifters trying them and others questioning the trend.[3][4][5]

claims.claim: Training the stretched position grows more muscle
claims.believers: Lifters say overloading the lengthened position is working for their delts, upper chest and triceps.[5]
claims.experts: Wikipedia describes long-muscle-length exercise as beneficial for hypertrophy, while a 2025 trial in trained lifters found lengthened partials and full range gave similar gains.[1][2]

claims.claim: Lengthened partials are a passing fad
claims.believers: One T Nation poster describes them as the latest science-based training fad.[3]
claims.experts: Researchers have published a controlled comparison showing similar adaptations to full range training.[2]

card.summary: Overloading only the stretched part of a rep; plausible in hypertrophy theory, thinly documented here.
card.note: Thin sources; no dedicated trials summarised.

quick.overview:
Lengthened partials are repetitions done only in the stretched portion of a lift. Lifters use them to load muscles at long lengths.

Hypertrophy overviews describe training at long muscle lengths as beneficial, but no dedicated trials were summarised here.
quick.mechanism: The technique aims to keep mechanical tension high while the muscle is elongated, which proponents link to growth.
quick.risks: Heavy loading in stretched positions can stress joints and connective tissue, as with other resistance training. No technique-specific harm data were identified.

chain: Reps done only in the stretched position
High tension on the muscle at long length
angle.text: Lifters add lengthened partials to build muscle in areas such as delts, chest and triceps. The technique works through training volume and tension at long muscle lengths rather than through any change to the body outside the gym.
